messages.content: use rides, rode, and riding in a short story about someone going to visit family.

a woman rides the train to see her aunt every month. last month, she rode with her brother. today, she is riding alone and looking at the town through the window. she has a book with her, but she wants to watch the journey for a while before reading.
which part is about the past?
last month, she rode with her brother. rode is the word for that past journey.
can rides be about something that happens often rather than right now?
yes. in she rides the train every month, it gives something she does again each month. is riding puts us with the journey happening now in the story.
what if she is not on a train today?
then change that part to a plan or leave it out. you could say: she will ride alone on her next visit. do not use is riding now if the story says she is still at home.
write the story with her at home today.
she rides the train to see her aunt every month. last month, she rode with her brother. today, she is at home and choosing a book for her next visit.
does choosing the book mean the train ticket is bought?
no. the story only says she is choosing a book. another detail would be needed to say what she has done about the ticket.
write a story with runs and ran. let the person run for a reason, not because the story says they run all day.

a boy runs to the garden door when his sister calls. she wants to show him a new flower, and he is happy to see it. later, he can tell his father that he ran outside to look. his father asks whether he was late for something. he says no. he just wanted to see what his sister had found. after that, he walks back inside and sits down to draw the flower.
put that part in the past.
later, he told his father that he ran outside to look. after that, he walked back inside and sat down to draw the flower.
does seeing him run tell the father he must have been late?
no. running can have different reasons. in the story, the boy wanted to see the flower. he was not said to be late.
can you make it clear that he runs only in that moment?
when his sister calls from the garden, he runs to the door. after seeing the flower, he walks back inside.
why is the sentence he runs different from he is always running?
always is about much more time than one run in a story. one moment is not enough to say he does it all the time.
answer simply.
one run is about one moment. always running is about much more time than that.
use builds, built, and building in a conversation about a toy house.

what is your sister doing? she is building a small house for her game. does she build often? yes, she builds something new on many days. what did she make before this? she built a garden wall for another story.
use days in the sentence about how often she builds.
yes, she builds something new on many days.
does built mean the old wall is gone?
no. built puts the work in the past. it does not say whether the wall is still there or has been taken apart.
ask my question simply.
does built mean the old wall is gone now?
write a short story where the old wall is used with the new house.

a child built a small wall for a garden game. later, she starts building a house and puts the old wall near it. her brother asks whether every part is new. she says no. the house is new, but the wall came from another game.
can using the wall again be part of making a new picture?
yes. something from an old game can have a place in a new one. new does not always mean every part was made today.
now ask the child what she wants to build next.
what would you like to build after the house is ready?
write a calm story using sleeps and slept. keep the father reading while the child sleeps.

a child sleeps near her father while he reads at the table. he keeps the room quiet. later, she asks whether he slept too. he says no. he read a few pages while she slept. she asks what happened in the story, and he can show her a picture of the garden it is about. they talk quietly for a moment, then she chooses another place to sit.
make it simple.
a child sleeps while her father reads. later, she asks whether he slept too. he says he read a few pages while she slept. then they look at a garden picture in his book together.
does the child sleeping mean everyone in the room was sleeping?
no. the father was reading. the story gives each person something different to do.
answer simply.
no. the child slept, and the father read.
make a short conversation for when she asks about his book.
did you finish the book? not yet. i only read a few pages. can you tell me about them? yes. this part is about a garden and the people who work there.
what part of that conversation gives us the fact that the book is not finished?
not yet and only read a few pages. he says there is still more to read.
answer simply.
not yet says he has not finished the book.
write a story about a child drawing a face with a mouth and ears. let someone ask about the drawing rather than say it must be wrong.

a child draws a face on a large page. the mouth is very small, and the ears are large. her father asks why she made them that way. she says the person in her story listens more than they talk. he asks whether a real person would have to look that way too. she says no. this is an idea for the picture, rather than a rule for every person who listens.
ask my request simply.
write about a child drawing a face with a small mouth and large ears, and a father asking why.
does having large ears tell us that someone listens well?
no. the picture has that idea, but the size of the ears of a real person does not tell us how well they listen.
answer simply.
no. the drawing is a story idea, rather than a fact about every person with large ears.
use the ears of a real person in the explanation.
the size of the ears of a real person does not tell us how well they listen.
why can the picture still work as a made up idea?
it can be a made up idea about the person in the story, rather than about every real person.
answer simply.
the drawing can give a made up idea without being a fact about every real person.
write a story about a doctor cooking with a daughter at home. keep it about the meal and their time together.

a doctor comes home and puts work things away before dinner. his daughter asks whether she can help make soup. he says yes and asks what she would like to do. she wants to choose the vegetables. they look at what is in the kitchen and choose a few for the meal. while the soup cooks, she talks to him about a game she played. he asks questions and listens. at the table, she says she likes having time when they do something together.
use told in a past story.
while the soup cooked, she told him about a game she played. he asked questions and listened.
does the story need to be about health because he is a doctor?
no. the request was about a family meal. his work can be one part of his life without choosing every conversation he has.
answer simply.
no. his work is one part of his life. the story can be about time at home with his daughter.
write a question he can ask about her game.
what did you enjoy most about playing it?
does that choose her best part of the game for her?
no. it gives her room to tell him. he is asking rather than saying he already knows.
ask my last question simply.
does that choose which part she liked most?
write a short conversation between a person who works at a bank and a teacher. they meet in a library, and they should talk about reading instead of work.

hello. are you looking for a book too? yes, i want a story for a quiet evening. what kind do you like? i enjoy stories about people learning something new. so do i. shall we look at these together? yes, then we can each choose one.
does meeting at a library mean both people work there?
no. they can visit a place without working there. their work at a bank and a school does not change just because they meet in another place.
answer simply.
no. visiting the library does not mean working there.
can they choose different books and still say they looked together?
yes. they can look together and choose different books. doing one part together does not make every later choice the same.
say it simply.
they can look together and still choose different books.
write one last line asking to talk about their choices later.
would you like to tell me about your book after you read some of it?
can that be a question without a specific day?
yes. it asks about the idea, but the people would still need to choose when to talk.
answer simply.
yes. the question does not give a day or hour.
in my made up picture, one animal has a red nose and blue eyes. help me write about only that animal without saying every animal is the same.
the animal in this picture has a red nose and blue eyes. these are details of this made up animal, rather than a rule for every animal.
say my request simply.
write about the red nose and blue eyes of the animal in my picture only.
can you make a small story about someone asking why i chose that color for the nose and eyes?

a child draws an animal with a red nose and blue eyes. her brother asks whether she saw one like that. she says no. she chose the color for her story. he asks what the animal does, and she says it helps people find the road home at night.
use color in a short answer.
she says she made the color choice for her story, rather than from an animal she saw.
does finding a road at night follow from having a red nose?
no. the red nose is one detail, and helping people find a road is another made up story idea.
answer simply.
no. the red nose is one detail, and helping people find a road is another story idea.
can i keep both ideas if i say it is made up?
yes. you can use both for this animal in your story while keeping them different from facts about all animals.
i drew five stars on a page. then i moved the whole page from the desk to the shelf. how many stars are on the page now?
still five, unless the drawing itself changed. moving the page does not add or take away a star.
now i draw one more star on the same page.
then there are six stars on the page.
if i take a picture of the page, are there now six more real stars in the sky?
no. you made a picture of the drawing. it does not add real stars to the sky.
write a small story where a child learns that difference.
a child draws six stars and takes a picture. his sister asks whether the picture made new real stars. he says no. the drawing still has six, and the sky was not changed by the picture.
make it simple.
a child takes a picture of six stars he drew. that makes another picture, rather than new real stars in the sky.
can he say there are six stars in each of two pictures?
yes. each picture can show the same six stars from the drawing. keep clear that the question is about pictures, rather than real stars in the sky.
answer simply.
yes. each picture can show the same six stars from the drawing.
i have butter, cream, and salt in the kitchen. if i call them all food, does that tell you how each one is used?
no. food gives a general group. you need more words to say what you want to do with butter, cream, or salt.
answer simply.
no. the general word food does not give every detail about how to use those things.
write a short conversation where someone asks before adding one to a meal.
should i add cream to this soup? i would rather have mine without it. then i can keep yours as it is and add a little to my own cup. that works for both of us.
does the conversation say cream must go in every soup?
no. it is one choice for one meal. another person or meal can have a different choice.
what if someone asks for more salt after trying the soup?
you can ask whether they want it only in their own food. do not change the whole pot before asking what the other people want.
give a question.
would you like salt only in your own cup, or should we ask the group about the whole pot?
can general words help without giving every detail?
yes. a general word can start the conversation, while more specific words give the details needed for the next choice.
can a room be cold while a drink is warm?
yes. cold and warm are about different things in that sentence. the room and the drink do not need to be the same.
write a short story with that idea and a blanket.

a woman sits in a cold room with a warm drink and a blanket over her legs. her friend asks whether she wants to move to another room. she says she is fine for a little while because she likes what she can see from the window. they talk until she finishes the drink, then go to the kitchen.
use what she can see.
she says she likes what she can see from the window.
does the fact that she likes the window mean she thinks the room is warm?
no. she can like the window and still think the room is cold.
answer simply.
she can enjoy one part and still know another part is not what she wants.
why did you not say she stayed there for the whole day?
the story only says a little while, then they went to the kitchen. saying the whole day would add a time not given in that story.
make that last answer shorter.
the story says a little while, not the whole day.
picoboi, i am going to give a fact, then ask a question. the cup is white. is the book blue?
you told me the cup is white. you did not tell me the color of the book, so i do not know whether it is blue.
can the question itself count as a fact that the book is blue?
no. asking whether it is blue leaves the answer open. i need more information before saying yes.
now i tell you the book is green.
then the book is green, and the cup is white, from the facts you gave.
what if i ask is the cup green too?
that is still a question. the cup was said to be white. i should not change it to green unless you give new information about it.
can you ask whether i want to change the cup fact?
do you mean the cup is green now, or are you asking whether it is?
i am only asking.
then the cup is still white in the information you gave. the book is green. your question did not change the cup fact.
write those two facts as a short sentence.
the cup is white, and the book is green.
